correspondences.rationale: Both denote a hard failure of a coherent transmitter laser that removes transmitted light.
Both denote a hard card-level equipment failure.
Both denote a soft, receiver-local degradation that adds a reception penalty.
Both denote incipient transmitter-laser ageing evidenced by upward bias-current drift.
Both denote a slow incipient decline in an optical channel's performance margin.
Both denote a physical fibre discontinuity that prevents optical propagation.
Both denote a hard amplifier or pump failure resulting in no amplifier output.
Both denote a disconnected optical jumper, patch cord, or connector.
Both denote excessive added attenuation on a fibre span.
Both denote a soft increase in amplifier noise figure that lowers OSNR.
Both denote an increase in differential group delay on the optical path.
Both denote a frequency offset of a WSS passband for one channel.
Both denote a rapid state-of-polarisation change that can exceed receiver tracking.
Both denote connector contamination that introduces optical loss or degradation.
Both are generic placeholders for an unspecified failure in infrastructure on which the relevant ODU path depends.
Both denote amplifier gain falling below its configured target.
Both denote incipient EDFA pump ageing evidenced by rising drive current.
Both denote wavelength-dependent, non-flat amplifier gain.
Both denote a hard failure of an OTN switch's cross-connect fabric.
Both denote an incorrect OTN cross-connect that sends an ODU to the wrong destination.
Both denote hard failure of a client port or its optic.
Both denote drift of a WSS channel's attenuation away from its setting.
Both denote hard failure of a WSS port, blocking traffic entering through that port.
Both denote absent or undetectably low optical signal at a receiver.
Both denote loss of OTU frame alignment at the line receiver.
Both denote pre-FEC errors above the degradation threshold while OTU framing remains aligned.
Both denote a fast polarisation change affecting coherent reception.
Both denote ODU-AIS travelling downstream on affected ODU paths.
Both denote rising transmitter laser-bias current as an ageing indication.
Both denote a gradual decline in channel margin.
Both denote reduced optical signal-to-noise ratio.
Both denote pump drive current rising to maintain amplifier gain.
Both denote a reduced optical signal-power state; A specializes it as input power.
Both denote loss of the incoming optical supervisory channel on a span.
Both denote an ODU delivered to the wrong destination by a cross-connect.
Both denote interruption of the client service.
Both denote only a brief client-service interruption during protection switching.
Both denote optical power measured at a line receiver.
A explicitly includes client errored seconds and standard performance monitoring; B is the corresponding 15-minute client counter.
Both denote channel OSNR as observed or estimated through coherent monitoring, although A also allows OCM measurement.
Both denote pre-FEC bit-error ratio at the coherent receiver.
Both denote differential group delay estimated or measured by coherent reception.
Both denote the rate of change of the received state of polarisation.
Both denote transmitter laser-bias current as a percentage of beginning-of-life current.
Both denote total optical power at an amplifier input.
Both denote total optical power at an amplifier output.
Both denote amplifier pump-drive current as a percentage of beginning-of-life current.
Both denote the client unavailable-seconds performance counter; B specifies 15-minute bins.
Both denote per-channel optical power measured by a ROADM optical channel monitor.
Both denote an EDFA optical amplifier resource.
Both denote an amplifier in the booster role at the transmitting end of an OMS.
Both denote an in-line amplifier at an intermediate amplifier site.
Both denote a pre-amplifier at the receiving end of an OMS.
Both denote an OTN switch with an ODU cross-connect fabric.
Both denote a client-facing port that maps client traffic into transport ODUs.
Both denote the ROADM resource used for per-degree WSS channel routing, though A specifically requires CDC capabilities.
Both denote one optical channel.
Both restrict impact to the observing receiver.
Both denote every channel in the affected multiplexed optical signal.
Both scope an equipment-health condition to the affected equipment unit itself.
Both denote a proper subset of multiplexed channels, with A specifically identifying channels at one band edge.
Both denote all affected ODUs traversing the relevant transport entity; B specifically frames them as ODUs through a switch.
Both denote a single ODU trail or connection.
Both denote one port, including all channels entering through one ROADM degree's input port.
Both denote the particular client service affected.
Both identify the local equipment unit that reports or contains the fault.
Both identify the particular local port reporting the fault.
Both denote the fibre span immediately upstream of the observing unit.
Both denote the immediately preceding amplifier in the upstream direction.
Both denote the physical input connection of the optical multiplex section.
Both denote any earlier fibre, amplifier, section input, or ROADM point on the signal path.
Both denote the remote line transmitter feeding the current receiver.
Both denote the remote receiver opposite the local transmitter.
Both denote either client-service endpoint, with B explicitly identifying the endpoint client ports.
Both denote an OTN switch or cross-connect located on the service's ODU path.
Both denote the working member of a protected ODU path pair.
Both denote the protection member of a protected ODU path pair.
Both denote the ODU path currently carrying the protected service.
Both denote baseline monitoring consisting of alarms and standard 15-minute counters.
Both denote the optional capability exposing optical input, output, and receive-power monitors.
Both denote advanced coherent-DSP and equipment-health telemetry.
Both denote OCM capability providing per-channel power and OSNR.
Both denote an abrupt hard fault causing traffic loss.
Both denote a degradation while traffic may continue.
Both denote a slow precursor trend before failure.
Both denote critical alarm severity.
Both denote major alarm severity.
Both denote minor alarm severity.
Both denote a reported condition that is not itself alarmed.
Both denote independent per-channel ROADM routing, with line-wide ingress conditions continuing on each routed channel.
